name: SeedVR2
plain: SeedVR2 (Wang et al., ByteDance Seed, 2025): upscales and restores photos and video frames x2 with a large diffusion transformer run for a single step; 3 B and 7 B versions, the 7 B runs on 16 GB with weight streaming (default, ~17 GB free host RAM). Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: SeedVR2 (Wang et al., ByteDance Seed 2025): one-step video restoration and super-resolution by a diffusion transformer (NaDiT, adversarially post-trained) on the latents of a causal 3-D VAE. `seedvr2-3b` and `seedvr2-7b` are the 3 B and 7 B transformers (same VAE); frames are restored one at a time.

papers.title: SeedVR2: One-Step Video Restoration via Diffusion Adversarial Post-Training

licence_notes: The converted weight files (bf16 transformer with the fixed prompt embedding, bf16 VAE) are hosted by fastforks under the originals' Apache-2.0 licence; NOTICE keeps the attribution and lists the changes.
limitations: Generative restoration: the output depends on `seed` (one CPU generator draws the VAE posterior noise and the diffusion noise, upstream's default 666); other seeds give other plausible details.
One frame per call: the clip mode of the original (temporal attention over 4n + 1 frames) is not used by this image API.

The input is padded on the bottom and right (replicate) so that `scale x` its size is a multiple of 16, and the output cropped back; the original centre-crops the resized frame to a multiple of 16 instead.
No colour fix: the authors' scripts optionally match the output colours to the input with StableSR's wavelet reconstruction (non-commercial code), which is not included.

The 3 B model needs ~7 GB for its weights plus the VAE's activations (~14 GB peak at 960 x 1696 output); `stream=False` keeps them resident; by default (`stream=True`, CUDA) they stay in ~6.6 GB of page-locked host RAM (~9 GB peak at that size).

The 3 B TensorRT measurement uses `stream=False` and fixed 64 x 64 input. Export with `export_onnx`, then build the engine in a fresh process. On 25 DIV2K crops the largest per-crop PSNR change was 0.109 dB. The largest single-pixel RGB channel difference was 0.627 on the [0, 1] scale.

The 7 B model's weights are 16.5 GB in bf16: it runs with the default `stream=True` (blocks in ~16.5 GB of page-locked host RAM; load fails with an error when less is free) or `quant="nf4"` (~4.6 GB resident); with `stream=false` and no quant it runs out of GPU memory.

The standalone 7 B compile benchmark compiles the VAE encoder and decoder, with the streamed transformer eager. On 25 DIV2K crops at 512 x 512 the largest RGB PSNR change was 0.0575 dB and the largest single-pixel channel change was 0.359.

The 7 B TensorRT measurement uses fixed BF16 VAE encoder and decoder plans with the streamed transformer in PyTorch. On the same 25 DIV2K crops at 512 x 512, the largest paired RGB PSNR change was 0.0710 dB. Latency was 2.696 s versus 2.712 s for portable.

`quant="nf4"` changes the generated detail: 23-27 dB PSNR against the bf16 output (3 B, 4 clips; 7 B: 26-31 dB, 2 clips), about as far as another `seed` (18-24 dB), with ~3.5x smaller transformer blocks.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: the restored (upscaled) image, `model.scale` x the input size, RGB in [0, 1]. `tile=` runs large images in overlapping tiles (as ComfyUI).

portable.note: Eager BF16, host-streamed transformer. Bounded single-frame VAE workspace on the 1024 x 1024 output. The largest paired PSNR difference across 13 DIV2K crops was 0.00047 dB.

kernels.note: The bounded single-frame VAE with the NF4 transformer. Three labeled DIV2K crops changed by less than 0.0001 dB PSNR.

quality.title: DIV2K validation, 4 centre crops 512 px, bicubic x2 LR -> HR, PSNR / SSIM (Y) / PSNR to the original
quality.protocol: SeedVR2 is a generative one-step restorer, so PSNR is only a fidelity check. Each of the centre 512 px crops of DIV2K validation HR images (a tiny subset: generation is slow) is downscaled with bicubic x2 (PIL) and restored x2 by the model, one pass; PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) on the Y channel of the uint8 output with a 2 px border cropped, averaged over the crops; PSNR to the original = RGB uint8 PSNR of our output against the authors' output of the same input and settings. The original is the authors' inference code, bf16. No perceptual metric (LPIPS) is given: the lpips package and its network weights are not part of the test environment.

original16.note: reference: plain bicubic x2 of the same LR crops = PSNR 29.01 dB / SSIM 0.8075 (a generative restorer scores lower: it re-draws detail and shifts tone); LPIPS not computed (package not installed in the test venv)

portable.note: reference: plain bicubic x2 of the same LR crops = PSNR 29.01 dB / SSIM 0.8075 (a generative restorer scores lower: it re-draws detail and shifts tone); LPIPS not computed (package not installed in the test venv)

quality.title: DIV2K validation, 25 bicubic x2 center crops of 64 x 64 LR pixels, RGB PSNR
quality.protocol: Every fourth DIV2K validation image. A 64 x 64 center crop of the official bicubic x2 input is restored at 128 x 128 and compared with the corresponding original pixels. PSNR uses RGB in [0, 1] and is averaged over the 25 crops. Both modes use resident BF16 weights and seed 666.

quality.protocol: First frame of each clip (clips of 2 to 10 frames, x2); PSNR of our output (RGB, uint8) against the authors' output of the same clip; there is no ground truth for these clips.
